description: We are engineering FUSION-AI, an autonomous space mission cyber-range trainer. Real outposts face engineering trade-offs between speed and security, where exposing Modbus, S7, or RDP risks remote takeover. Our Python engine emulates adversary loops against flat networks to prove this impact, then trains operators to build resilience via pfSense—isolating IT from critical OT systems using strict blocking rules and encrypted OpenVPN tunnels with certificate-based MFA & Suricata IPS/IDS monitoring.
summary:
FUSION-AI is a modular cybersecurity intelligence and cyber-range training platform designed to help organizations identify security weaknesses, understand cyber threats, and strengthen critical infrastructure resilience.

Through an isolated virtual laboratory, FUSION-AI simulates adversarial reconnaissance and vulnerability discovery against vulnerable systems, demonstrating how exposed services and unsegmented networks can create opportunities for attackers.

The project demonstrates a defense-in-depth approach using pfSense network segmentation to separate WAN, IT, and simulated OT environments, combined with controlled VPN access and certificate-based authentication. Its architecture can be extended with multi-factor authentication, Active Directory or FreeRADIUS, Wazuh SIEM, and Suricata IDS/IPS for centralized monitoring and deeper traffic inspection.

For this challenge, a virtual laboratory represents a hypothetical space mission ground infrastructure. No real NASA systems are accessed or tested.

Our vision is to make practical cybersecurity more accessible through an open-source approach, helping small businesses, hospitals, public institutions, and critical infrastructure operators build safer and more resilient environments.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & WHY IT MATTERS

Future lunar and Martian habitats will depend on interconnected digital infrastructure, including communications, power management, environmental monitoring, and operational technology (OT).

These environments introduce a critical engineering challenge: maintaining operational availability while protecting systems against cyber threats. With communication delays between Mars and Earth reaching over 20 minutes one-way, mission operators must be prepared to identify and manage incidents without depending on immediate ground support.

FUSION-AI explores this challenge through practical cybersecurity analysis and isolated virtual simulations.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Offensive Cybersecurity Analysis — Python Engine

FUSION-AI orchestrates a modular security assessment pipeline covering reconnaissance, service discovery, enumeration, vulnerability verification, and risk correlation. It integrates tools such as Nmap, HTTPX, WhatWeb, Katana, Gobuster, FFUF, and Nuclei.

For this demonstration, Metasploitable represents a hypothetical vulnerable ground infrastructure server inside an isolated virtual laboratory. The platform organizes findings into a chronological attack timeline and risk reports, illustrating how exposed services and insufficient segmentation can increase an organization's attack surface.

2. Defense-in-Depth Architecture — pfSense

The defensive scenario demonstrates a three-interface network architecture: WAN, IT, and simulated OT.

Firewall policies restrict unauthorized communication between network segments. Remote administration can be protected through encrypted VPN connectivity, individual certificates, and controlled user credentials.

The architecture is designed to support future integrations such as multi-factor authentication, Active Directory, FreeRADIUS, Wazuh SIEM, and Suricata IDS/IPS.

These integrations represent potential extensions and are not claimed as active components unless demonstrated in the current laboratory.

BENEFITS & TECHNOLOGY

Built with Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, pfSense, OpenVPN, and VirtualBox, FUSION-AI connects offensive security analysis with defensive infrastructure design.

Its broader vision is to make cybersecurity assessment and practical security education more accessible to small businesses, hospitals, clinics, public institutions, and critical infrastructure operators.

FUSION-AI demonstrates that resilience is not simply about preventing every attack. It is about limiting exposure, restricting unauthorized access, detecting threats, and preventing an individual compromise from becoming an organization-wide incident.
